semantic_correction.stem: A client recovering from shoulder surgery can move the affected arm through part of the prescribed range but needs assistance to complete the motion. Which exercise description is most accurate?

options.A: Active range-of-motion exercise means the client moves the joint through the prescribed range using the client's own muscle activity without physical assistance.
options.B: Passive range-of-motion exercise means another person moves the joint through the prescribed range while the client does not actively perform the movement.
options.C: Active-assisted range-of-motion exercise means the client performs part of the movement and receives assistance to complete the prescribed range.
options.D: Resistive range-of-motion exercise means the client actively moves the joint against applied resistance to increase muscle strength during the exercise.

semantic_correction.rationale: C is correct. The current NCBI Bookshelf Open RN Nursing Fundamentals, 2nd edition, defines active-assist range-of-motion exercise as a client's joint receiving partial assistance in movement from an outside force. The same source defines active range of motion as movement of a joint by the individual performing the exercise. These definitions distinguish a client who can initiate or perform part of a movement but needs help to complete the prescribed range from a client performing the movement independently. Passive range of motion is performed for the client rather than by the client's active muscle effort, while resistive exercise adds resistance to active movement for strengthening. Therefore the stem most directly describes active-assisted range of motion. A is incorrect because the client in the stem cannot complete the movement independently. B is incorrect because the client is actively participating rather than remaining passive. D is incorrect because the need described is assistance to complete motion, not resistance against active movement.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Differentiate active-assisted range of motion from active, passive, and resistive exercise based on how much of the movement the client performs independently and whether assistance or resistance is provided.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed the absolute-word and structural cueing pattern, rebuilt all four exercise definitions to parallel length and specificity, freshly verified the current NCBI/Open RN ROM definitions, and preserved one uniquely correct active-assisted ROM response.

audit_findings_append.source_locator: Nursing Fundamentals 2nd ed. Master Glossary and Mobility chapter — ROM definitions
audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item tests recognition of active-assisted ROM with one clearly best answer, parallel distractors, current source verification, and no absolute-word or length cue.

option_audit.A: Incorrect. Active ROM is performed by the client without physical assistance; the stem states that help is needed to complete the range.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Passive ROM is performed for the client rather than combining client effort with partial assistance.
option_audit.C: Correct. It directly matches the NCBI/Open RN definition of active-assisted ROM as client movement supplemented by partial outside assistance.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Resistive exercise adds resistance to active movement for strengthening rather than helping the client complete an otherwise unattainable range.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. C uniquely matches partial client effort plus assistance; A lacks assistance, B lacks active client participation, and D adds resistance rather than assistance.
cueing_check: All four options are parallel exercise definitions of comparable length and structure; prior absolute-word cues were removed and the correct response is not uniquely detailed.
